### Building a New PC – A Step‑by‑Step Guide Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order for safety and best results. | # | Step | What to Do | Tips | |---|------|------------|------| | 1 | **Plan & Budget** | • Decide what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office, etc.).
• Set a budget (CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, case, PSU, peripherals). | Use online PC builders (PCPartPicker, BuildMyPC) to check compatibility and prices. | | 2 | **Gather Tools & Workspace** | • Phillips‑head screwdriver (magnetic tip).
• Anti‑static wrist strap or mat.
• Small container for screws.
• Clean, flat surface. | Avoid carpet; static can damage components. | | 3 | **Choose Components** | • **CPU** – Intel Core i5/i7 or AMD Ryzen 5/7.
• **Motherboard** – compatible socket, chipset, form factor (ATX, mATX, mini‑ITX).
• **RAM** – DDR4/DDR5, 16 GB minimum for gaming, 32 GB+ for content creation.
• **GPU** – NVIDIA RTX 3060/3070 or AMD RX 6600/6700, depending on budget.
• **Storage** – NVMe SSD (500 GB–1 TB) + optional SATA HDD for bulk.
• **Power Supply** – 550–750 W 80+ Gold (or higher for high‑end GPUs).
• **Case** – ATX/mATX/mini‑ITX, good airflow, cable management. | Check the motherboard’s CPU socket and RAM type before buying. | | 4 | **Prepare the Case** | • Remove side panels.
• Install standoffs for the motherboard (usually pre‑installed, but double‑check). | Keep the case open while you work. | | 5 | **Install the CPU** | • Open the CPU socket latch.
• Align the CPU (triangle marker) with the socket.
• Gently place it, then lock the latch. | Don’t force; the CPU will fit snugly. | | 6 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install Cooler** | • If the cooler doesn’t have pre‑applied paste, apply a pea‑size amount on the CPU.
• Mount the cooler according to its instructions (attach brackets, screw in).
• Connect the cooler fan to the CPU fan header. | Use a low‑profile cooler for small cases. | | 7 | **Install RAM** | • Open the RAM slots’ clips.
• Align the notch on the RAM stick with the slot and press firmly until the clips click. | Install in the recommended slots (often 1 & 3 for dual‑channel). | | 8 | **Mount the Motherboard** | • Align the motherboard with the standoffs and I/O shield.
• Screw it down with the provided screws. | Double‑check that all screws are tight but not over‑tightened. | | 9 | **Install Storage** | • Mount NVMe SSD in the M.2 slot (usually a small screw).
• For SATA SSD/HDD, use a drive bay or mounting bracket. | Label cables if you have multiple drives. | | 10 | **Install Power Supply** | • Place PSU in the case (bottom or top, depending on case).
• Secure with screws.
• Route cables: 24‑pin ATX, 8‑pin EPS, PCIe power for GPU. | Keep cables tidy; use Velcro ties. | | 11 | **Install GPU** | • Remove the appropriate expansion slot covers on the case.
• Insert GPU into the top PCIe x16 slot.
• Secure with screws.
• Connect 6‑ or 8‑pin PCIe power cables. | Ensure the GPU is fully seated; it should click into place. | | 12 | **Connect Front Panel & Peripherals** | • Connect the case’s front‑panel connectors (power button, reset, USB, audio) to the motherboard headers.
• Connect the power button to the motherboard’s power header. | Refer to the motherboard manual for exact pin layout. | | 13 | **Cable Management** | • Tidy up cables using Velcro ties or zip ties.
• Route cables through the case’s cable‑management holes. | Good airflow = better cooling. | | 14 | **First Boot** | • Connect a monitor, keyboard, and mouse.
• Power on the system.
• Enter BIOS/UEFI (usually F2, Del, or Esc).
• Verify CPU, RAM, storage, and GPU are detected. | If nothing shows, double‑check power connections and seating. | | 15 | **Install Operating System** | • Create a bootable USB with Windows 10/11 or Linux.
• Boot from USB, install OS, and install drivers (chipset, GPU, Wi‑Fi). | Keep the OS installation media handy for future updates. | | 16 | **Update & Test** | • Install all drivers and Windows updates.
• Run a stress test (Prime95, 3DMark, FurMark) to ensure stability.
• Monitor temperatures (HWMonitor, MSI Afterburner). | If temperatures are too high, re‑apply thermal paste or improve airflow. | | 17 | **Final Touches** | • Re‑attach side panels.
• Install any additional fans or RGB lighting.
• Set up your workspace and peripherals. | Keep the system in a dust‑free environment. | --- #### Quick Checklist - [ ] CPU + cooler installed - [ ] RAM seated - [ ] Motherboard mounted - [ ] PSU installed - [ ] GPU seated - [ ] Storage installed - [ ] Front panel connectors wired - [ ] Cables managed - [ ] First boot successful - [ ] OS installed - [ ] Drivers updated - [ ] Stress test passed --- #### Common Pitfalls & Fixes | Issue | Likely Cause | Fix | |-------|--------------|-----| | No display | GPU not seated or power cable missing | Re‑insert GPU, connect power | | BIOS not detecting RAM | Wrong slot or not fully seated | Re‑install RAM in correct slots | | Overheating | Poor airflow, insufficient thermal paste | Add case fans, re‑apply paste | | System won’t power | PSU not connected or faulty | Check PSU cables, try a different PSU | | Blue screen on boot | Driver conflict or bad RAM | Update drivers, run MemTest86 | --- #### Resources - **PCPartPicker** – Build lists, price tracking, compatibility checks. - **YouTube Channels** – Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware for visual guides. - **Manuals** – Keep motherboard, case, and PSU manuals handy; they’re often PDF downloads on the manufacturer’s website. Enjoy your new build! If you hit a snag, let me know the specific issue and I can help troubleshoot.
message.reasoning: User asks: "How to build a new PC?" They want instructions. We can provide a step-by-step guide. No function call needed.
